title: Provider-neutral tracker seam and its first GitHub adapter
summary: Adds a new `tracker` module to the `osf` crate: a provider-neutral `Tracker` trait (read ready items, write state, write a recap, report capabilities), a pure ready rule that decides which read item may be dispatched, a finishing-write helper that checks capabilities before writing state then recap, and an in-memory `FakeTracker` test double. Alongside it lands the first adapter, `github_tracker`, which drives GitHub Issues and Projects v2 through the installed `gh` CLI: every request is one `gh` invocation whose argv and JSON payload are built by pure functions and whose response is read by a pure parser, with a `RealGhRunner` that spawns the process, drains its pipes and enforces a timeout. Nothing existing is modified beyond two `pub mod` lines in `lib.rs`; the whole change is additive.

nodes.label: Tracker trait
nodes.subtitle: read_ready / write_state / write_recap / capabilities
nodes.summary: The seam between the factory and a work tracker. Four methods, object-safe, with the contract that an adapter must not filter by the ready status itself and that a blocked write records the cause before moving the status.

nodes.label: Tracker types
nodes.subtitle: WorkItem, WorkItemId, WorkState, Capability
nodes.summary: The vocabulary the seam speaks: a work item with its status, closed flag and blockers; a `provider:repo#item` id that round-trips through `FromStr`; the five work states with their blocked causes; and a three-valued capability report.

nodes.label: Ready rule
nodes.subtitle: dispatchable / pick
nodes.summary: Pure decision logic kept out of every adapter: an item is dispatchable when it is open, its status is ready and every blocker is closed. `pick` returns the first dispatchable item, or a typed reason for each skipped one.

nodes.label: Finishing writes
nodes.subtitle: require_capabilities / finish_run
nodes.summary: Checks the states a run needs and the recap against the tracker's reported capabilities, then writes the state and the recap, stopping at the first failure and naming the step that failed.

nodes.label: FakeTracker
nodes.subtitle: in-memory double, records every call
nodes.summary: A `Tracker` that answers from memory and records each call as plain data, with scripted failures per operation and per state. It does no I/O, so a whole engine-style run can be exercised without a process, file, network or clock.

nodes.label: GitHubTracker
nodes.subtitle: impl Tracker for GitHubTracker<R: GhRunner>
nodes.summary: The adapter itself: a thin loop over a `GhRunner`. It reads the project's status field and options, pages ready items, resolves one issue's project item id, posts a cause comment for a blocked state, and writes the single-select field value.

nodes.label: Request builders
nodes.subtitle: read_ready_payload, project_status_payload, item_id_payload, mutation_payload, comment_payload
nodes.summary: Pure functions that build the argv and the JSON body of every request, plus the GraphQL query and mutation strings. Being pure, they are pinned by tests without running anything.

nodes.label: Response parsers
nodes.subtitle: parse_items_page, parse_project_status, parse_item_id, parse_write_result
nodes.summary: Pure parsers for every response. A malformed item that is not in the ready status is kept as a skipped item whose status text begins with `unreadable:`, so one bad non-ready item does not fail the page; a malformed ready item is an error.

nodes.label: GhRunner
nodes.subtitle: trait GhRunner / RealGhRunner
nodes.summary: The one place a process is reached. `RealGhRunner` spawns the program, drains stdout and stderr on their own threads, writes stdin, and kills the child after a timeout (60 seconds by default).

nodes.label: gh CLI
nodes.subtitle: installed command-line tool
nodes.summary: The installed `gh` program. Every adapter request is exactly one invocation of it, with the GraphQL body on standard input.

nodes.label: GitHub GraphQL API
nodes.subtitle: Issues and Projects v2
nodes.summary: The service behind `gh`: project items with their single-select status, issue blockers, and the mutation that moves an item's status.

nodes.label: Tracker tests
nodes.subtitle: tracker_fake_run, tracker_neutral
nodes.summary: A full engine-style run over the double, and a source scan asserting the seam's own files name no provider or tool.

nodes.label: Real runner tests
nodes.subtitle: tracker_real_runner
nodes.summary: Drives the real runner against a fake `gh` shell script in a temp folder: argv and stdin are passed through, stderr is trimmed on a non-zero exit, a missing program and a hanging program are reported, and the timeout is enforced.

flows.summary: How a run reports its outcome: capabilities are checked first, a blocked state posts its cause comment before the status moves, and the recap is written last.

messages.note: The recap is written only after the state write succeeded; the first failure stops the run and names its step.

steps.heading: A provider-neutral seam
steps.body: The trait, its vocabulary, the ready rule and the finishing writes land as one module.

detail.text: The seam is four methods over a small vocabulary, with the ready rule and the finishing writes kept out of every adapter.

steps.heading: The first adapter
steps.body: GitHubTracker implements the seam as a thin loop over a runner.

detail.text: The adapter implements the seam and reaches the outside world only through the runner.

steps.heading: Pure halves, one impure edge
steps.body: Argv and payload builders and response parsers are pure; only the runner spawns a process.

detail.text: Request builders and response parsers are pinned by tests without running anything; the runner is the one place a process is reached.

steps.heading: Reading and picking
steps.body: Verify the status field, page the items, then let the rule decide.

steps.heading: Writing state and recap
steps.body: Capabilities first, then the cause comment, the status move and the recap.

detail.text: A blocked state posts its cause comment before the status moves, and the recap is written only after the state write succeeded.
